text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Vietnam has called for greater efforts from members of the Non-Aligned Movement for global nuclear disarmament and reform of the United Nations.
-- Vietnam's Minister for Agriculture and Rural Development has begun a four-day visit to Egypt to boost agricultural cooperation.
-- Ho Chi Minh City's labour department has announced plans to use 3.4 million man-power days of compulsory labour this year to develop public utility projects.
-- U.S companies had pledged to invest more than $1.0 billion in 66 projects in Vietnam by mid-March.
-- The Czech Republic has pledged $700,000 to help Vietnam improve its railway system in 1997.
-- Twenty-four people have been killed and 50 injured during the last six weeks while trying to dismantle war-era bombs to retrieve and sell parts.
-- The Prime Minister has instructed high-ranking officials to take part in courses on administrative management.
-- Harvesting of the winter-spring rice crop in the Mekong Delta might be affected by early rains this year.
